RetailMax Inc. - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the RetailMax Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, participants are required to utilize the handset function to mute background noise. Please also note, today's event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, and thank you for joining us today to discuss RetailMax Inc.'s results for the Q3 2024. Joining me on today’s call are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; and Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements, which are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

With that, I’ll turn the call over to Johnathan.

Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I’m pleased to report RetailMax Inc.'s performance for the Q3 2024. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities and delivered solid results despite the challenging macroeconomic environment.

Today I will cover four key aspects of our performance. First, our overall company performance highlights. This quarter really highlights the resilience and strategic execution of our brick-and-mortar-first model in a dynamic retail environment. We've achieved strong top-line growth, margin improvements, and solid advances in our omnichannel efforts, even with consumer spending cooling under ongoing inflation around 3.2% CPI year-over-year.

Our consolidated net sales hit $2.85 billion, up 8.2% from last year and beating our guidance by a solid margin. This is our ninth straight quarter of positive comparable store sales, landing at 5.4%, which picked up from 4.1% in Q2. Behind that were 3.2% higher store traffic and a 2.1% rise in average transaction value, thanks to smart in-store merchandising and upgrades to our loyalty program. For perspective, that's well ahead of the National Retail Federation's 2.8% average for core brick-and-mortar peers.

By segment, Home & Garden, making up 42% of sales, surged with 11.3% comps, powered by demand for our value-focused private-label items like Essentials Home, which grew units 25% as housing stabilized and DIY spending rose 15% year-over-year per Nielsen. Apparel & Accessories, 35% of the mix, posted 6.8% comps from back-to-school strength and our bigger plus-size offerings, grabbing 12% more share against Macy's and Kohl's. Electronics & Entertainment, 18% of sales, managed 4.2% comps despite some pullback in big-ticket TVs and gaming due to upgrade delays.

Gross margins grew 110 basis points to 38.4%, the best in three years, thanks to 220 basis points from supply chain wins like RFID across 85% of our 1,250 stores, cutting shrinkage 18% and trimming days of supply to 42 from 58. Private-label share reached 28% from 24%, adding 90 basis points via better sourcing from Vietnam and Mexico after tariff easing. We also gained 40 basis points with tight pricing on promos, keeping markdowns at 14.2% versus the 16.5% category norm per Kantar.

SG&A dipped 60 basis points to 24.1% of sales through AI-driven labor scheduling that boosted associate productivity 9% with better shift planning, much like Target's shop-in-shop boosts. Adjusted EBITDA rose 22% to $285 million at a 10.0% margin, diluted EPS hit $0.72 beating estimates by $0.05, and free cash flow shone at $410 million, funding $150 million in buybacks and a 12% dividend increase to $0.28 per share.

Regionally, Sunbelt areas like Florida, Texas, and the Carolinas—38% of stores—saw 7.9% comps from population shifts and tourism rebound, with sales per square foot up 14% in growth spots like Austin and Phoenix. Midwest and Southeast, 45% of footprint, got 5.6% comps on value hunting as wages beat inflation. Northeast urban stores, 17%, softened to 2.1% comps from 18% office vacancies per CBRE hurting quick buys, but BOPIS jumped 32% to tap suburban demand.

We're pushing our 'Stores as Hubs' strategy harder, opening 12 next-gen 25,000 square foot urban prototypes with micro-fulfillment that outperformed legacy stores by 15% in sales per square foot right away. Omnichannel now 28% of revenue from 22%, with curbside at 65% of digital orders. Sustainability plays like recycled apparel boosted Gen Z loyalty signups 20% via Customer 360 insights.

Moving to our second key area, e-commerce sales growth year-over-year. Our digital channel keeps delivering strong results in a tough macro for physical retail. E-commerce sales came in at $800 million this quarter, up 22% reported and 24% constant currency, marking 11 quarters straight of double-digit gains, beating the U.S. retail e-commerce index's 12% per Census Bureau.

Digital now 28% of our $2.85 billion total net sales, up from 23% last year and nearing our 30% FY2025 goal. This puts us in line with Macy's 25-30% mix and ahead of Kohl's low-20s. GMV reached $900 million, with third-party sellers up 35% to 15% of digital GMV.

Traffic was key, with site and app visits up 28%, driven by 40% better paid search efficiency—CPC down 15% via Google Ads tweaks and SEM for terms like 'same-day delivery furniture' and 'curbside apparel pickup.' Organic search rose 18% from SEO on long-tail queries for private labels like Essentials Home, boosted 50% in visibility after our headless commerce shift to Adobe Commerce Cloud.

Mobile led with 62% traffic and 68% conversions, up from 55%, thanks to our Q1 app relaunch with AR try-on for apparel and 3D planners for home, lifting app sessions 32% and conversion from 3.2% to 4.1%. AOV stayed at $145 with Salesforce Einstein AI upsells raising add-to-cart 12% via bundles like Levi's with our tees.

Omnichannel shone, BOPIS up 45% to 25% of digital fulfillment, ship-from-store up 30% using our 1,200 stores as hubs. This sped delivery—85% same- or next-day—and cut digital fulfillment costs to 8.5% from 10.2%, with RFID accuracy over 98% in 80% of stores.

U.S. drove 26% growth to $640 million, strong in apparel +29% and home +22%, especially Sunbelt. International, 20% of digital, grew 12% to $160 million; Canada +18% with Shopify Plus for French personalization. Europe +8% despite UK/Germany caution, but Q4 TikTok Shops should hit 20%+. APAC pilots in Australia via BigCommerce grew 50% month-over-month.

This reinforces 'Stores as Hubs'—we acquire customers 25% cheaper than pure e-tailers like Wayfair, with 40% BOPIS converting to store add-ons. Digital-first LTV tops $1,200 over three years, up 15%, justifying $250 million digital capex like Nevada DC automation and Zipline drones.

Next, store performance, particularly sales per square foot, one of our core productivity measures—net sales divided by average selling square footage. It cuts through store count noise to show how well we're using our 45 million square feet across 1,200 locations amid e-commerce shifts.

In Q3, we hit $512 per square foot, up 7.2% year-over-year and 3.1% from Q2's $497, beating our 5% target and topping mid-tier peers. TJX is $450-$460, Macy's under $300, Ulta around $550 in beauty. This ties to 4.8% comps, 60% traffic-driven and 40% higher AUR at $48.50 from $46.20.

Regionally, Northeast and West Coast urban hit $578, +11%, from high-ABW traffic in New York/San Francisco and Store 2.0 remodels shrinking space 15% while lifting conversion to 28% from 25%. Southeast at $465, +2.1%, hit by Florida tourism and Carolinas hurricanes. Midwest $498 with home goods up 12% on 8% space.

Trend: Q4 2022 $485, Q1 2023 $492, Q3 2024 $512—now 6% above pre-COVID adjusted. Categories: Apparel (42% sales) $420 +9% on 7.2x turns from 6.5x; footwear/accessories $680 on displays; home $380 from $350 via MaxHome private label +22% units.

Our plan has three pillars. Footprint: closed 25 underperformers (400k sq ft below $350), opened 15 express 8,000 sq ft stores at $650—shrinking average size to 36,500 by FYE 2024, 10% reduction no sales loss.

Tech: RFID at 65% cuts shrink to 1.2% from 1.8%, AI planograms with Shelfgram up sell-through 14%; BOPIS 18% store sales adds $75/sq ft; mobile POS in 200 stores cuts lines 40%, impulse +8%.

Experiential: shoppertainment like beauty bars, chef demos up dwell to 22 min, AUR +15%; inventory at 42 days supports 42.1% gross margins.

Guidance: Q4 $525-$535 (5-8% comps), full-year $505 +9%. Risks holiday traffic dips per Nielsen 2-3%, but BOPIS and new stores offset. Physical retail wins on conversion when done right.

Finally, our marketing initiatives, focusing on digital marketing effectiveness. In this omnichannel era, digital accelerates our 1,200+ stores in North America/Europe, driving traffic, BOPIS, and tickets via targeted campaigns.

We spent $42 million on digital, +18% YoY or 12% of SG&A, yielding 6.2x blended ROAS from 4.8x. Paid search (Google/Bing) 8.1x on 'kitchen remodel near me,' +22% store conversions via Google Analytics 4. Social (Meta/TikTok) 5.4x, TikTok #HomeRefreshHacks 1.2M impressions +14% traffic for millennials/Gen Z.

CAC fell 15% to $28/new loyalty member (18M active) via lookalikes from Essentials Rewards. Email opens 42%, Klaviyo geo-fenced 3.5x CTRs. Digital drove 28% comps, BOPIS +32% to $185M or 22% e-comm—BOPIS spend 1.8x more in-store.

Post-iOS 14.5, our CDP on Tealium/Manhattan POS uses zero-party data from Wi-Fi/app for Trade Desk DCO—1,200 variants for personas like urban renovators. Geofencing 1-mile around 450 U.S. stores: 4.5M pushes +17% footfall per Placer.ai. HomeEssentials Media Network added $8M from CPG shelf data.

U.S. (75% spend) suburban like Atlanta/Dallas +25% ROAS on drive-time. Europe (250 stores UK/Germany) 4.9x despite GDPR/2% slowdown, +19% BOPIS London via TikTok/Snapchat AR. Canada 7.2x bilingual SEO.

Ahead of Bed Bath or Wayfair, Q4 25% budget to CTV (Roku/Fire TV) shoppables 2x visits; quiz funnels cut waste 22%. Q3 ROAS 6.5-7x, full-year saves $15-20M.

Digital fuels stores in our hybrid model.

We are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Michael to provide more details on our financial results.

Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer:
Thank you, Johnathan. Good morning. I'll provide a more detailed review of our financial performance for the Q3 2024.

Revenue: Our total revenue for the quarter was $2.85 billion, an 8.2% increase compared to the same period last year.

Gross Margin: Gross margin was 38.4%, primarily driven by supply chain efficiencies from RFID rollout, higher private-label penetration, and pricing discipline on promotions.

Operating Expenses: Operating expenses were $687 million, representing 24.1% of revenue.

Net Income: Net income was $180 million, or $0.72 per share.

Cash Flow: We generated $450 million in cash flow from operations.

Inventory: Inventory levels are currently at 42 days of supply, reflecting optimized stock levels and improved turns.

We are maintaining a strong balance sheet and are well positioned to invest in our growth initiatives.

Now, let's open the line for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. As a reminder, participants are required to utilize the handset function to mute background noise. Our first question comes from Ben Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Ben Smith (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation pressures on your sales?

Johnathan Hale:
Thanks, Ben. Inflation has been a headwind, no doubt, with CPI at 3.2% weighing on discretionary spend, but our value positioning and private-label strength have helped us outperform. Comps at 5.4% beat the industry by a wide margin, led by Home & Garden where DIY demand held up despite broader softness. We've seen traffic resilient at +3.2%, and our regional wins in Sunbelt markets show consumers prioritizing essentials and home improvements. Our pricing discipline kept markdowns low, protecting margins while capturing share— we're navigating it well through omnichannel synergy and store hubs.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen (JPMorgan):
What are your expectations for same-store sales growth in the next quarter?

Michael Chen:
Good question, Lisa. We're raising our FY24 comp guidance to 4.5-5.5%, and for Q4 specifically, we see same-store sales in the 5-8% range, supported by holiday momentum, BOPIS surges, and our new express stores. Risks like traffic softness from inflation-weary shoppers are there per Nielsen data, but tailwinds from remodels and digital traffic should drive us through.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Alex Rivera with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera (Morgan Stanley):
Thanks. On digital marketing, how sustainable is that ROAS improvement, and any updates on CTV pilots?

Michael Chen:
Alex, great to hear from you. The 6.2x ROAS is sustainable and building, thanks to privacy-safe tech like our CDP and DCO— we've cut CAC meaningfully with first-party data. CTV pilots on Roku and Fire TV are showing 2x store visits over linear, tied to real-time inventory. We're ramping to 25% of Q4 budget there, expecting 6.5-7x blended ROAS as back-to-school and holidays kick in. It's a traffic engine for our stores.

Operator:
Thank you. There are no further questions at this time.

Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, we are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our long-term strategy. Thank you for your continued support.

Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations:
This concludes today's call. Thank you for joining us.

aspect_summary.Digital marketing effectiveness: Digital spend $42M (+18% YoY, 12% SG&A) yielded 6.2x ROAS (from 4.8x), with paid search 8.1x, social 5.4x; CAC down 15% to $28/new loyalty member; drove 28% comps, BOPIS +32% to $185M; Q4 CTV ramp-up for 6.5-7x ROAS.

aspect_summary.E-commerce sales growth (YoY): E-commerce sales $800M, +22% reported/+24% constant currency YoY (11th straight double-digit quarter); 28% of total sales (from 23%), nearing 30% goal; traffic +28%, mobile 62%, BOPIS +45% to 25% fulfillment; U.S. +26%, international +12%.
